confirmed.error: invalid_grant: Session does not have required client
confirmed.failure_layer: Host OIDC refresh, followed by inability to renew worker token

timeline_local.event: Cluster access recovers after user login

interpretation: The exact Keycloak error means the refresh path cannot find the required authenticated client session. It is not explained solely by a 30-minute ID token lifetime. Claims from the replacement refresh token do not establish the lifetime of the lost session.
unconfirmed_hypotheses: Server-side offline client session idle/max policy or revocation
Client-session cache/persistence inconsistency or server restart
Concurrent refreshes from independent host processes may contribute; causality is unproven
next_steps: Administrator should inspect REFRESH_TOKEN_ERROR for realm rcpepfl / client runai-cli at the incident timestamps, offline-client timeout policy, and session cache events
For unattended evaluation, evaluate an administrator-supported RunAI user access key or service account instead of a personal browser SSO session
Centralize token refreshing into one writer and let monitoring consumers use the staged short-lived token to reduce concurrent refresh races

editor_and_concurrency_followup.mechanism: client-go v0.31.14 OIDC uses an in-process mutex around refresh and then persists refreshed tokens; independent kubectl processes are not serialized by that mutex.
editor_and_concurrency_followup.assessment: Concurrent refresh is a credible investigation direction. Current evidence confirms multiple backend refresh-capable consumers, but does not prove VS Code participation or causation of the server-side error.
recommended_controlled_test: Centralize refresh in the credential sync service; other automation consumers use only staged short-lived tokens
Independently compare periods with the local Kubernetes extension/attach disabled and enabled across multiple 30-minute refresh boundaries
Record sanitized refresh timestamps, caller PID, and kubeconfig write timing; never log tokens
